title: merge: a HOLD at a superseded head is released by the same friend's typed verdict at head (#2550)
body:
`nova-merge batch` carried a HOLD forever once the branch moved past the head it
bound to. Measured 2026-09-22 02:25Z-13:50Z on schema fixed-table-form: 57
consecutive ticks took the same 16 approved cell pull requests and dropped every
one of them --

    BATCH DROP #1551 reason="head 5adf9cb212a8 carries an unreleased HOLD"
    who=emma hold=comment:5767845547 source=comment-rule held_at=67712d4eb59a
    carried=yes at=2026-09-21T21:35:02Z conf=-

-- where held_at is a head the branch had moved past and the current head carried
four typed `DISPOSITION who=Emma head=5adf9cb2... verdict=APPROVE score=10/10`
comments from that same friend. members=none, so the integration branch was empty
and GitHub refused the pull request. 0 of 16 landed in 11.5 h with read debt at 0.

Two causes, both here:

1. ParseComment never read a typed APPROVE at all. A comment carrying
   `DISPOSITION ... verdict=APPROVE` fell through to the untyped branch and came
   back as a PENDING comment -- a typed verdict read as evidence of nothing, and
   then as a second reason to drop the member.
2. UnreleasedHolds only ever asked whether a hold was released, never whether it
   had been superseded. A hold at a head that is gone is the last word its author
   left about a commit nobody can look at.

releaseCarriedHolds is deliberately narrow and touches CARRIED holds only: a hold
AT the current head is untouched, and a comment still releases nothing there. An
APPROVE at some other superseded head releases nothing -- release keys on the
head. A who=unknown hold is untouched: an untyped hold-shaped line has no author
to match and binds to the current head anyway.

The second ask on the issue, both halves, in the same file:

- a typed APPROVE's head= is kept as typed and compared by headMatch, the same
  prefix rule a typed HOLD's head= gets, so `head=5adf9cb2` and the whole
  40-character object name are the same head on both verdicts;
- a releasing APPROVE must be the WHOLE line (dispositionWholeLine): first token
  exactly DISPOSITION, every token after it a key=value field, no stray prose, no
  repeated key. A HOLD keeps the lenient parse on purpose -- tightening the
  parser on the holding side would turn a sloppily typed HOLD into a non-hold,
  and a rule about smuggling must never fail open on the side that stops a merge.

The controls. internal/merge/carriedhold_test.go is a ten-row table over the
whole pipe (forge JSON, ParseComment, the fold): the issue's four rows, the live
#1551 shape, the 12-character prefix, the smuggled mid-line APPROVE, another
friend's APPROVE, and two rows that hold the line this must not cross -- a
comment releases nothing at head, and an untyped bold HOLD fails closed. Four
rows were red on dev. cmd/nova-merge/carriedhold2550_test.go drives the verb and
reproduces the break exactly on dev (`members=none dropped=1`), with its negative
twin: take the APPROVE away and the gate still drops the member, still carried=yes.

SPEC-DECIDE.md's release section said "a comment releases nothing, typed or not"
without qualification, so the amendment is written there beside it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
